name: Single-Arm Tricep Pushdown
description: The single-arm tricep pushdown is a unilateral cable isolation exercise for the triceps. Training one arm at a time allows independent focus on each triceps, eliminates strength imbalances, and enables a greater range of motion with wrist rotation at the bottom for a more complete tricep contraction. The lateral and medial heads are most active, with the long head contributing based on the grip angle used.

execution.starting_position: Attach a single handle to the high pulley of a cable machine. Stand facing the machine, holding the handle in one hand with the elbow bent at 90 degrees and tucked at the side.
execution.setup_instructions: Set cable to high pulley. Attach a D-ring single handle. Stand close enough to the machine so there is tension on the cable with the elbow at 90 degrees.
steps: Step 1: Hold the single handle with one hand, elbow tucked at the side at 90 degrees.
Step 2: Keep the upper arm stationary throughout — only the forearm moves.
Step 3: Exhale and push the handle downward by extending the elbow until the arm is fully straight.
Step 4: Hold the lockout, then inhale and return the forearm to 90 degrees.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on extension; inhale on return.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbow drift forward or away from the side during the push
Rotating the torso toward the working arm
safety_considerations: Keep the wrist in a neutral position — do not flex the wrist at the bottom
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at the bottom; return to 90-degree elbow bend at the top.
coaching_cues: Elbow stays glued to your side — it is the pivot point
Straighten all the way — do not stop short of full lockout
